# Cases

One place per matter: the case numbers (Aktenzeichen) in your mails, letters and todos hold together what belongs to one case — who it is
owed to, what is open after your payments, the next instalment or deadline, and where to pay (with a GiroCode).

**Stage 1 of the port.** Generated by Zeff's `scripts/port-cases.mts`.

- **Its data stays where it is.** Its stores are the built-in's own tables (`cases`, `case_sources`, `case_parties`), adopted:
  nothing is copied, and the built-in and the port see the same cases.
- **The overview.** The lambda `cases.overview` reads the stores and the kernel (the money ledger, your contacts' names and accounts,
  the rows the cases are in) and works the overview out with the built-in's own core (`lambdas/_lib.mjs`). Its screen
  (`views/overview.html`) is the built-in's template made of the view language; a case's GiroCode is the kit's `<girocode>`.
- **Finding the cases** (stage 2): the flow `cases.detect` (every 30 minutes, 7–21 o'clock) — its lambda `cases.detect` works the plan
  out with the built-in's own core (the case numbers in your mails, letters and todos, read through the kernel), the flow writes it
  through the stores (`cases_by_key`: the cases table by the case number; `sources`), `cases.link` gives new sources their case's id.
- **The AI's summaries** (stage 2): the flow `cases.summarize` (hourly, 7–21 o'clock; at most 8 a run) — `cases.summarize-plan` picks
  the cases due and builds what the AI reads (your instructions if you changed them: System → Prompts), the kernel's `ai.json` answers,
  `cases.summarize-apply` checks it and moves it on by the payments since, `people.contacts` finds or makes the creditor and who
  collects it, `cases.summarize-parties` keeps what you chose yourself.
- **Your payments** (stage 2): the flow `cases.match` (hourly) — `cases.match-plan` works out with the built-in's own core what each
  booking out not matched yet is (a todo's transfer and its case, a payment you ticked off, one read twice, evidence of what it pays
  anyway), the flow keeps it through the kernel (`money.pay`, `money.confirm`, `money.settle`, `todos.done` — its `money` and
  `todos` permissions); `cases.settle` moves a case on whenever its payments change (the ledger's event `ledger.changed`).
- **Warnings before a plan lapses** (stage 2): the flow `cases.warn` (daily at 8) — an instalment ten days late with nothing paid since: a
  todo to pay it, once, with the transfer on it (the kernel's `todos.add`).
- **The bank bar** (stage 2): a statement read from a file (with the Revolut plugin: the kernel's `bank.import`), the bank connection
  (Enable Banking — `bank.status`, `bank.save`, `bank.auth`, `bank.sync`: the bank is a driver of the kernel, its bookings shared
  data, lib/bank); after either the flows `cases.match` and `cases.warn` run and the overview is read again.
- **A case's own page**: the lambda `cases.case` gives the built-in's page data, `views/case.html` draws it (the database's detail page).
- **The cases database's rows**: the source `cases` (lambda `cases.records`) stands in for the built-in's — the same records, so the
  database reads on after the switch.
- **The switch** (*Switch to the plugin* on the Cases card): the plugin on, its package installed under System (its flows allowed), the
  cases database's overview and a case's page the plugin's screens, the built-in off. Your cases stay in the same tables.
- **With the built-in off**: People, the first look, a Revolut statement and the bank still see and match your cases — they ask the kernel who keeps them (`lib/cases/there.ts`) and run this plugin's flows.
